questions.question: What key limitation of traditional DLA methods motivates the gDSA task?
questions.ground_truth_excerpt: Traditional document layout analysis (DLA) methods offer only a superficial parsing of documents, focusing on basic instance detection and often failing to capture the nuanced spatial and logical relations between instances.

questions.question: Which existing dataset does GraphDoc primarily derive from?
questions.ground_truth_excerpt: Our GraphDoc Dataset is primarily derived from the DocLayNet dataset, which contains over 80,000 document page images spanning financial reports, user manuals, scientific papers, and legal regulations.

questions.question: Under what license are enhanced versions of the DocLayNet-based dataset permitted to be redistributed?
questions.ground_truth_excerpt: In accordance with the License CDLA 1.0, users are permitted to modify and redistribute enhanced versions of datasets based on the DocLayNet dataset.

questions.question: Why does GraphDoc only consider relations within the same page rather than across pages?
questions.ground_truth_excerpt: Due to page limitations of DocLayNet, we will only consider relations within the same page and not those across pages.

questions.question: What two pooling-based branches make up the Relation Feature Extractor in DRGG?
questions.ground_truth_excerpt: The object queries and object feature representations calculated at each decoder layer are fed into independent relation feature extractors, processed through two independent pooling layers and MLPs.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the auxiliary relation prediction head in DRGG?
questions.ground_truth_excerpt: This auxiliary relation head focuses solely on determining whether a relation exists between two document elements, without classifying the type of relation, acting as a stabilizer that minimizes false positives.

questions.question: How is the final relational prediction combined from the main and auxiliary relation heads?
questions.ground_truth_excerpt: The final relational prediction is computed by multiplying the main relation predictor's output and the auxiliary relation head's output element-wise, retaining only confidently predicted relations.

questions.question: What optimizer and learning rate settings were used to train DRGG?
questions.ground_truth_excerpt: We trained the model with the AdamW optimizer using a batch size of 4, an initial learning rate of 1x10^-4, and a weight decay of 5x10^-3.

questions.question: What multi-scale image resizing strategy was used during training?
questions.ground_truth_excerpt: The shorter side of each input image was randomly resized to one of several lengths between 480 and 800 pixels, while the longer side did not exceed 1333 pixels.

questions.question: Which backbone-detector combination achieves the highest mAP on the DLA task?
questions.ground_truth_excerpt: The DRGG framework integrated with the InternImage backbone and RoDLA detector achieves mAP of 81.5%, surpassing all other combinations.

questions.question: Which relation category is hardest for DRGG to detect, and what AP score does it achieve?
questions.ground_truth_excerpt: The reference relation remains challenging, with the highest AP being 18.8% achieved by ResNeXt with RoDLA; our model achieves an AP of 16.8% in this category.

questions.question: What happens to performance when the relation feature extractor is replaced with a single linear layer?
questions.ground_truth_excerpt: The feature extractor significantly outperforms a linear layer replacement across all metrics, with DLA mAP dropping from 81.5 to 79.9 and mAPg@0.75 dropping from 56.3 to 42.3.

questions.question: How does raising the IoU threshold from 0.5 to 0.95 affect gDSA performance?
questions.ground_truth_excerpt: At the highest IoU threshold of 0.95, the model achieves only 18.4 mRg@0.95 and 36.5 mAPg@0.95, demonstrating significant challenges in capturing precise alignments.

questions.question: Which document domain achieves the highest mAPg@0.5, and which performs worst on mRg@0.95?
questions.ground_truth_excerpt: Laws and Regulations achieve the highest mAPg@0.5 with 63.2, while Patents perform worst, with mRg@0.95 at 17.5, due to their dense and complex layouts.

questions.question: How does adding logical relations alongside spatial relations affect mRg and mAPg?
questions.ground_truth_excerpt: When logical relations are included alongside spatial relations, mRg@0.5 drops from 32.1 to 26.7, while mAPg@0.5 improves from 49.5 to 57.5.

questions.question: What four groups are document elements categorized into when building the hierarchical structure?
questions.ground_truth_excerpt: Annotations are grouped into four categories: elements with direct structural relations, non-textual content within the logical structure, elements lacking direct associations, and references only (footnotes).

questions.question: What proportion of the GraphDoc dataset underwent human verification, and how many pages were reviewed per domain?
questions.ground_truth_excerpt: Extensive human verification and refinement cover approximately 58.5% of the dataset, reviewing 4,852 pages of Government Tenders, 12,000 pages of Financial Reports, 6,469 pages of Patents, and 8,000 pages from other domains.

questions.question: What two limitations does the paper acknowledge about the DRGG approach?
questions.ground_truth_excerpt: Our model structure focused only on visual modality input without multi-modality consideration, and the dataset and approach were primarily designed for single-page documents, with multi-page extension left unaddressed.

questions.question: What two main sources of error are identified in DRGG's qualitative relation predictions?
questions.ground_truth_excerpt: Errors arise primarily from ambiguity in densely populated layouts where elements lack clear alignment, and from misclassification and inaccurate bounding boxes at the DLA stage propagating to relation prediction.

questions.question: What improvements does the paper suggest to reduce DRGG's relation-prediction errors?
questions.ground_truth_excerpt: The authors suggest incorporating multimodal embeddings combining visual and textual features, improving the DLA backbone, integrating post-processing with contextual cues, and extending DRGG to multi-page relational understanding.
